facts.title: Why this car belongs
facts.explanation: The A310 carried Alpine beyond the compact A110 into the sporting grand-tourer market. The V6 road coupe retained a lightweight polyester body and backbone chassis while giving the angular four-seat design the six-cylinder performance central to its identity. It represents an important stage in Alpine’s transition from rally-focused berlinettes to French performance GTs.

media.caption: Alpine A310 V6 identified as a 1980 car at Capesthorne Hall in 2014. The narrow road body, four-headlamp nose and original-style three-stud wheels represent the early V6 design. Photo year, sunroof and exterior condition do not establish the selected brochure’s four-speed transmission, tune or mechanical originality. No wide-bodied Pack GT or competition conversion is substituted.

cars.specification_market: Original Renault Communication launch dossier dated 25 February 1991, embargoed to 19 March 1991. Gallery contains cover, press photographs and six text leaves: text pages 1–3 and Annexe 2/page 5 visually read. Launch table and narrative both specify 2975 cc; the 2015 factory retrospective’s 2963-cc/1990 wording is not substituted. Selected standard road A610, not Albertville, Magny-Cours, Le Mans competition or tuned car. No separate GTA record is added while same-lineage counting remains unresolved.
cars.summary: The A610 developed Alpine’s rear-engined GT concept into a substantially revised turbocharged road car. A reinforced backbone structure and bonded composite body accompanied revised suspension, strengthened transmission and ventilated brakes with ABS. Its three-litre V6 and pop-up-headlamp design make it a distinctive culmination of Alpine’s original performance-GT era.

Selected GTI-6 column, separate from XSi, automatic cabriolet and lighter Rallye. Native BHP/MKg labels retained without relabelling or calculated conversion. October 1998 range brochure M/CP1101 supplies period body/gearbox context only. No early five-speed S16/ACAV, BTCC, Maxi or Rallye competition specification.
cars.summary: The 306 GTI-6 is a defining Peugeot hot hatch, pairing a two-litre 16-valve engine with the unusually close-ratio six-speed manual developed by Peugeot Sport. Its responsive steering and compliant suspension established the balanced road-driving character that Peugeot continues to celebrate in its GTI heritage.

facts.title: Why this car belongs
facts.explanation: The 306 GTI-6 is a defining Peugeot hot hatch, pairing a two-litre 16-valve engine with the unusually close-ratio six-speed manual developed by Peugeot Sport. Its responsive steering and compliant suspension established the balanced road-driving character that Peugeot continues to celebrate in its GTI heritage.
